notes: The manual's 'row 1' is the numbered breadboard line crossing the ravine; in the catalogue's naming this is column 1, with the top bank (1t) left of the ravine and the bottom bank (1b) right of it.
LED anode (A, long leg) is in 1t.e and cathode (C) is in 1b.f, straddling the ravine.
Resistor leg 1 is in 1b.g, on the same strip as the LED cathode. Leg 2 is in 5b.g, a free column on the same side of the ravine.
Wire 1: male end in 1t.a, on the LED anode strip. Female end on the Pi 3V3 pin. Wire 2: male end in 5b.h, on the resistor's second-leg strip. Female end on the Pi GND pin.
The resistor value is not given, so no value prop is set. 3V3 with an LED and a series resistor is within the LED's current limits for a typical resistor.
The Raspberry Pi model is not specified, so raspberry-pi-3 is used for its 3V3 and GND ports. The tutorial says to use any GND pin.
